newsitem.title: UK: Pearson loss could top 200 million stg - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pearson loss could top 200 million stg - paper.

text.p: Losses by British media and leisure group Pearson Plc at a U.S. subsidiary may top 200 million stg, the Sunday Times newspaper said.
Pearson, due to report its 1996 results on Monday, said on February 13 that an accounting problem at its Penguin USA unit may lead to a charge against 1996 profits of as much as 100 million stg.
The Sunday Times said a pending legal action by the American Booksellers Association (ABA) could double that to 200 million stg.

Lawyers representing the ABA claim that by offering selective discounts to early payers, Pearson broke the terms of a 1996 legal order ending a dispute between ABA booksellers and Penguin USA, the Sunday Times said.
The Independent on Sunday newspaper said Pearson's new chief executive Marjorie Scardino had ruled out the sale of its television business.
The Independent on Sunday said Scardino viewed the television operations as central to Pearson's future.
Scardino, who moved to the top job at Pearson in January from its 50 percent-owned Economist magazine, has said the group's performance is not good enough.

Share analysts looking to Pearson's results for guidance on possible disposals believe the figures will provide a platform for Scardino to outline her vision for a group which has long been accused of lacking focus.
Analysts expected Pearson's investment banking interests or tourist attractions in its Tussauds Group could be sacrificed as part of the new management's drive for focus.
Pearson's assets include the Financial Times newspaper, television production businesses, a 50 percent share in merchant bank Lazard Brothers and Madame Tussaud's waxworks.
